title: Effective field equations with stochastic initial conditions
abstract: The evolution of quantum field expectation values from an initial non-equilibrium quantum state can be followed numerically using the Truncated Wigner technique. It can track non-perturbative quantum phenomena, such as false vacuum decay, in real time with promising results. Nevertheless, it is an approximate method subject to quantum loop corrections. The extension of Truncated Wigner into a fully fledged effective field equation approach is discussed here, including corrections from higher loops and higher momenta.
summary: This paper develops an advanced method to calculate the evolution of quantum fields starting from non-equilibrium states by extending the Truncated Wigner Approximation. It systematically incorporates quantum loop corrections into effective field equations, providing theoretical tools for studying phenomena like vacuum decay beyond simple classical approximations.
main_problem: The primary goal is to extend the Truncated Wigner technique into a fully fledged effective field equation approach by systematically incorporating quantum loop corrections.
main_result: The authors show that the naive TWA is valid at one loop, and higher-order corrections are non-local and difficult to implement, suggesting a systematic but challenging path toward full quantum treatment.
method: The work combines the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) with the effective action formalism derived from the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral, allowing for loop expansion calculations.
model_or_system: The analysis uses a general Klein-Gordon scalar field $\phi$ with an interaction potential $V(\phi)$, applicable to systems like Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC) and modeling phenomena such as false vacuum decay.
key_observables: Field expectation values ($\langle \hat{\phi} angle$), the Wigner functional, and loop-corrected effective actions $\Gamma[\phi_1, \phi_2]$.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on initial state widths ($\Omega_k$ vs. $\omega_k$) and involves comparing results across different loop orders (one-loop, two-loop).
main_assumptions: The TWA is an approximation valid only for Gaussian initial states; higher-order corrections are non-local and computationally demanding.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of two-loop diagrams contributing to the effective action and show how loop correction integrals exhibit oscillatory or saturating behavior over time.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the TWA for non-equilibrium evolution, deriving the one-loop corrected field equation, and then analyzing the complexity and results of incorporating higher (two-loop) quantum corrections systematically.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework to bridge classical stochastic methods (TWA) with full quantum field theory loop corrections, which is crucial for accurately modeling non-equilibrium dynamics in many-body systems like BECs.
